Series::TraverseAccessor::find_not¶

Back to Series::TraverseAccessor API Reference

Signatures¶

TraverseMatch Series::TraverseAccessor::find_not(const Series& mask) const;
TraverseMatch SeriesTraverseProxy::find_not(const Series& mask) const;

What It Does¶

find_not(mask) returns the coordinates of every position where mask is false. It is find_all with mask.logical_not().

It is the single-mask member of the boolean-combinator family alongside find_and and find_or. For a predicate that is a plain equality, find_neq is the more direct spelling; use find_not to invert a mask that came from arbitrary logic.

Shape rules and gradient behavior match find_and.

Parameters¶

mask (const Series&)

A condition shaped like the traversed Series. Matched positions are the ones where it is not true.

Returns¶

TraverseMatch Row-major coordinates and matched values of the false positions.

Example¶

auto grid = pluss::make_series({
    {10.0, 4.0, 7.0},
    {2.0, 9.0, 6.0},
    {8.0, 1.0, 5.0},
});

auto below_five = grid.traverse.find_not(grid.ge(5.0));

std::cout << "count=" << below_five.count() << "\n";
std::cout << below_five.coords();

Output¶

count=3
pluss::Series(shape=[3,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[0, 1],
  [1, 0],
  [2, 1]]

find_not(grid.ge(5.0)) is the same set as find_le would give for < 5 — the values 4, 2, 1.
